subject: Demo recap — proposed trial scope, success metrics & timeline (Celestia Systems)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@celestiasystems.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — quick recap and ask after today’s demo

Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning — the streaming demo and routing fallbacks were particularly helpful. Quick recap from our side and a request for a proposed trial plan: 

Key business goal: cut NLU/response latency for our customer support assistant by 40% while keeping answer accuracy within current thresholds.

Primary evaluation questions:
- Can Redwood hit 150 reqs/s with p95 latency < 250ms for 512-token prompts?
- How does the KV cache affect cold-start user flows?
- Are there any output-quality regressions when using the quantized variant you demoed?

Next ask: can you send a proposed trial/PoC scope with success criteria, timeline (4–6 week preferred), and owner assignments? We’ll need this for internal sign-off and to align our security folks.

Security note: our security team will want a short list of evidence (SOC2, data-at-rest encryption, RBAC) and confirmation that test data can be synthetic or internally scoped — no production PII.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up tomorrow if helpful.

—Elena
Elena Torres
Head of AI Platforms, Celestia Systems
elena.torres@celestiasystems.com
[Attachment: celestia_requirements_v1.pdf (PDF, 124KB)]

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear goals. Attached is a compact trial plan that maps to the evaluation questions you listed and includes ownership, timeline, and minimal infra requirements. High-level summary below; full plan attached (redwood_trial_plan_v1.xlsx).

Proposed scope (4 weeks, optional week 5 buffer):
- Week 0: Kickoff, access provisioning, test data ingestion (synthetic dataset + redacted logs)
- Week 1: Baseline runs (your current model) + Redwood standard config to measure raw throughput/latency
- Week 2: Performance tuning — batching, KV cache, quantization profile A/B
- Week 3: Quality validation against your prompt set; automated evals + manual review of 200 samples
- Week 4: Run acceptance tests, handover docs, and recommended production config

Success criteria (suggested):
- Throughput: sustained 150 reqs/s for 90% of a 1-hour load window
- Latency: p95 < 250ms for 512-token average prompts
- Quality: automated BLEU/ROUGE/QA accuracy within 2% of baseline; no critical regressions in 200-sample manual review
- Stability: < 1% error rate over a 24-hour soak test

Owners and points of contact:
- Redwood PM / Trial lead: Stephanie Nguyen (stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai)
- Solutions engineer (setup & tuning): Aditya Rao (aditya_rao@redwood.ai)
- Customer lead: Elena Torres (elena.torres@celestiasystems.com)

Access & logistics: we will provision a dedicated sandbox on our hosted stack or a private VPC depending on your preference. We can avoid any production PII — synthetic + redacted logs will be fine.

Estimated credits: small hosted trial (up to 2M tokens) — we’ll provide an initial credit allocation on sign of the trial plan; we can cover additional analysis under a scoped add-on.

Attachments: redwood_trial_plan_v1.xlsx (workbook with week-by-week tasks), poc_runbook.md (runbook excerpts).

If this looks good I’ll loop in Aditya and Rishi to confirm kickoff availability and security evidence. Would you be available for a 30-min kickoff on Wed or Thu next week?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Product Manager, Trials & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood_trial_plan_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 56KB)]

Hi team — technical notes from the infra side: 

- Sandbox isolation: we will provision a dedicated VPC and customer-only service accounts. We will provide a short checklist for network egress rules.
- Test data: synthetic/redacted logs are fine; we recommend a 100k-line synthetic corpus plus a 200-sample manual review set (we’ll supply a generator).
- Perf testing: to get realistic 150 reqs/s results we’ll run a phased load: 20m warmup with KV priming, then 60m steady load. I recommend using the quantized 8-bit variant for one A/B arm and the baseline FP16 for the other.
- Observability: we’ll enable token-level tracing and a per-route latency dashboard during the run; we’ll export the raw traces for your team to ingest.

I’ve attached a short infra checklist. Let me know if the network team needs additional details and I’ll set up a short tech call.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
